tr.f: For blocked heart arteries, when a stent is not the best option.
tr.d: A healthy blood vessel is used to build a new route around the blocked part, so blood reaches the heart muscle again.
j: Angiography and tests, then the plan explained to you and your family
Surgery, followed by close monitoring in the ICU
Walking, breathing exercises and reviews until you are back to routine

tr.f: To see inside the heart arteries, and open a narrowing from the inside.
tr.d: A thin tube shows exactly where an artery is narrowed. If needed, a balloon opens it and a stent keeps it open.
j: ECG, echo and a clear reason for the test
A thin tube through the wrist or groin, usually without general anaesthesia
Medicines, a short stay and lifestyle changes

tr.f: For a valve that leaks or has become tight.
tr.d: Your own valve is repaired whenever possible. If not, it is replaced with a tissue or mechanical valve, chosen with you.
j: Echo to see how the valve works, and the choices explained
Repair or replacement surgery
Recovery plan and, if needed, blood thinner follow-up

tr.f: For heart defects children are born with, and those that develop later.
tr.d: Holes in the heart and other defects can often be corrected. Parents are walked through every step, in plain words.
j: A gentle consultation with the child and parents
Surgery planned around the child
Growth and heart checks as they grow up

tr.f: For selected patients who may benefit from smaller cuts, and for more complex heart conditions.
tr.d: Where it suits the patient, surgery through smaller cuts can mean less pain and a faster return home. Complex and repeat surgeries are planned in detail.
j: Detailed scans and a plan made for you
Surgery by the approach that suits you best
A recovery plan matched to the operation

tr.f: For blocked leg arteries, aneurysms and varicose veins.
tr.d: From swollen, aching veins to arteries that cause leg pain when you walk, treatment ranges from stockings and medicines to surgery.
j: Doppler scan of the legs
The right treatment for the vessel, from simple to surgical
Walking plan and follow-up scans

tr.f: For conditions of the lungs, chest wall and the space around the lungs.
tr.d: As a cardiothoracic surgeon, Dr. Yadav also operates on the lungs and chest, often working with chest physicians.
tags: Fluid or air around the lung
j: CT scan and breathing tests
Thoracic surgery
Breathing exercises and reviews

tr.f: For symptoms, risk factors like diabetes and BP, or a second opinion before surgery.
tr.d: A full consultation, the tests you actually need, and honest advice on whether you need treatment at all.
j: Your story, your reports, your worries
Examination, ECG and other tests if needed
A clear plan, or reassurance

tr.f: Urgent heart care, monitoring after surgery and rehabilitation.
tr.d: Close monitoring after surgery, then a step-by-step plan to get you home and active again. In an emergency, call 108 or 112 first.
j: A clear plan before you go home
Reviews in the first weeks
Back to work, walking and daily life

symptomsSpots.p1: Tightness, heaviness or burning in the chest, sometimes spreading to the arm, jaw or back, especially on walking or climbing stairs.
symptomsSpots.p2: This can be a sign of narrowed heart arteries. It needs a proper check, usually with an ECG and other tests.
symptomsSpots.u: Sudden or severe chest pain, with sweating or breathlessness? Call 108 or 112 now.

symptomsSpots.p1: Getting out of breath with less effort than before, needing more pillows at night, or waking up gasping.
symptomsSpots.p2: A weak pump, a leaking or tight valve, or a lung problem can all cause it. Tests help find which.
symptomsSpots.u: Breathless at rest, or lips turning blue? Call 108 or 112 now.

symptomsSpots.p1: A thumping, fluttering or skipping feeling in the chest, sometimes with dizziness.
symptomsSpots.p2: Often harmless, but sometimes a rhythm problem. An ECG or a 24 hour Holter can record it.
symptomsSpots.u: Palpitations with fainting or chest pain? Call 108 or 112 now.

symptomsSpots.p1: Feeling light-headed on standing or exertion, or passing out without warning.
symptomsSpots.p2: A narrow valve or a rhythm problem can reduce blood flow to the brain. It should always be checked.
symptomsSpots.u: Face drooping, weak arm, slurred speech? These are stroke signs. Call 108 or 112 now.

symptomsSpots.p1: Cramping in the calf or thigh that comes on with walking and eases with rest. Cold feet or slow-healing wounds.
symptomsSpots.p2: This can mean narrowed leg arteries. A Doppler scan helps.
symptomsSpots.u: Sudden cold, pale, painful leg? Call 108 or 112 now.

symptomsSpots.p1: Bulging blue veins, heaviness or aching after standing, itching or darkening skin near the ankle.
symptomsSpots.p2: These are varicose veins. Treatments range from stockings to surgery.
symptomsSpots.u: Sudden swelling and pain in one leg? It can be a clot. Seek urgent care.

symptomsSpots.p1: Puffiness around the ankles or feet that is worse by evening and leaves a dent when pressed.
symptomsSpots.p2: It can come from the heart, kidneys, veins or medicines. A check-up finds the cause.
symptomsSpots.u: Swelling with breathlessness at night? See a doctor the same day.
